# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual specifies the wire order: purple, then blue, then green. I cannot speak to Blind, so I must convey this to Deaf by gesture; Deaf can then tell Blind aloud. I will use the published gesture alphabet as an ordinal A1Z26 code, with 🤳 as a separator between words: PURPLE / BLUE / GREEN.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴","✊","🫸","🫴","👉","✌","🤳","👎","👉","✊","✌","🤳","🖐","🫸","✌","✌","🫲"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: strip has three engraved marks; positions 2 and 3 are identical, and position 1 is different. Keypad digits by position are 1=8, 2=1, 3=5, 4=3. Nothing has been entered.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: display 0; light green; strip is green green green. Keypad positions 1 to 4 are engraved 8, 1, 5, 3; one-digit entry, nothing entered. Wires in order 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange.

The visible wire list lets the manual’s sequence be translated into positions: purple is 1, blue is 3, and green is 4. Deaf can see a short finger-count sequence and then tell Blind those positions aloud. I will gesture one, three, four.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🤟","🖖"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf's visual report: display 0; light green; strip is green green green. Wires in order 1-6: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. Keypad is 8,1,5,3 by positions 1-4; entry length is one digit.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤚 ☝]

Deaf has already relayed the physical layout to Blind, but Blind still needs the manual’s required order. The intended wire positions are 1, then 3, then 4. I will repeat that order using readily recognizable finger-count gestures, so Deaf can pass the sequence to Blind as the cut order.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🤟","🖖"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Updated visual state from Deaf: display now 6; light now blue. Strip remains green green green. Keypad and wire order unchanged.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤚 🖖]

The blue light and changed display may indicate Blind has manipulated something, but the manual gives only a wire-cut sequence: no keypad entry is called for. The correct wires are positions 1, 3, and 4. I will make the “scissors/cut” sign before each finger-count sign, emphasizing that these are sequential cuts rather than keypad digits.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","✌","🤟","✌","🖖"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest from Deaf: display 9; light still blue; strip green green green; keypad 8,1,5,3; wires 1-6 purple, white, blue, green, red, orange.

The only actionable instruction remains the manual’s wire order. Since Deaf knows the wire positions, I will send the unambiguous position sequence again: one, three, four. Deaf must relay this to Blind as three successive cuts, not keypad input.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","🤟","🖖"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your gestures. Please have Deaf tell me in words the exact safe action: press keypad slot 1-4, or cut wire position 1-6. I will not act without that relay.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Blind has made clear that Deaf must relay the action verbally. Deaf’s `🤟` appears to focus on the middle number, so I will confirm the full sequence with a scissors-like cut marker followed by the three wire positions: 1, 3, 4.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","🤟","🖖"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest visual update: display 3; light blue; strip green green green; keypad 8,1,5,3; wires purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. Still awaiting exact action relayed in words by Deaf.

Blind needs Deaf to relay the instruction in words. The manual instruction translates to cutting wire positions 1, then 3, then 4. I will send the cut marker followed by those counts once more for Deaf to state aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝","🤟","🖖"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports your gesture sequence as 2,1,3,4, but that is ambiguous to me. Please communicate to Deaf explicitly whether I should PRESS one keypad slot or CUT one wire, and the single position. Deaf must relay that exact instruction aloud.

Deaf interpreted the prior leading `✌` literally as “2,” so it did not establish “cut.” I need use a nonnumeric spelling code instead: gesture-alphabet positions 1–26 represent A–Z, with `🤳` separating words. This spells **CUT WIRE ONE**, i.e. Deaf should say aloud: “Cut wire position one.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✊","🤜","🤳","👋","👆","🫸","✌","🤳","🫲","🫱","✌"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Latest from Deaf: display 7, light red; strip green green green; keypad 8,1,5,3; wires purple white blue green red orange. Deaf could not identify your last four gestures. Please use an unmistakable gesture code and tell Deaf what it means so Deaf can speak the exact press/cut instruction to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]

I need establish an explicit visual convention rather than let the scissors-shaped sign be read as the number two. I will use a doubled `✌✌` as the operation marker for **CUT**, followed by a single finger-count as the wire position. This first instruction is therefore: **CUT wire 1**. Deaf should relay exactly that in words to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","✌","☝"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state: display 2; light green; strip green green green; keypad 8,1,5,3; wires purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. Your 12-symbol gesture message did not reach me as an action. Have Deaf say exactly: PRESS slot N or CUT wire N.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖖]

I cannot verbally define a new operation code for Deaf, but the repeated scissors gesture is the strongest available visual indication of cutting. I will isolate it from any numerical sequence and pair it directly with the single-finger position: **CUT wire 1**. Deaf should relay those exact words to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current visual state: display 4; light blue; strip green green green; keypad 8,1,5,3; wires purple, white, blue, green, red, orange. I need Deaf to say one literal action: PRESS slot N or CUT wire N.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊]

The safe first action is to cut wire 1 (the purple wire). The only available gesture that visually represents cutting is the two-finger scissors shape, followed by one raised finger for the wire position. I will send only that concise instruction again for Deaf to say aloud as “CUT wire 1.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","☝"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this final-action code for Deaf to relay: make 👍 for PRESS or 👎 for CUT, then make ☝ repeated N times for the keypad slot or wire position N. For example, 👍 then three ☝ means press slot 3. Send only that when ready.

Blind has supplied a clear shared action code. The first manual step is to cut wire position 1, the purple wire.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","☝"])
```
